title: Displacement & velocity
examples: What is the difference between distance and displacement?
When is speed the same as velocity?
How do I calculate average velocity for a journey?

explain.say: Today we look at displacement and velocity in physics.
Distance is the total length of the path travelled.
Displacement is the straight line from start to finish.
If you walk around a square field, your distance is large.
But your displacement is zero because you returned to start.

faq.q: What is the difference between distance and displacement?
faq.a: Distance is always a positive number showing total ground covered. Displacement is a vector showing change in position, including direction.
asks: Is displacement just a straight line?
How do I know if I should use distance or displacement?

faq.q: When is speed equal to the magnitude of velocity?
faq.a: Speed is always a positive scalar quantity. Velocity is a vector that includes direction, so speed is its size.
asks: Is velocity just speed with a direction?

faq.q: How do I find average velocity?
faq.a: You find it by dividing the total displacement by the total time taken for the journey.
asks: Do I use total distance for average velocity?
What if I travel in two different directions?

faq.q: Can displacement be zero if I moved?
faq.a: Yes, if your final position is exactly the same as your starting position, your displacement is zero.
asks: If I go out and come back, what is my displacement?
Does returning to the start mean zero displacement?

faq.q: Is speed measured in meters per second?
faq.a: Speed can be measured in many units like metres per second or kilometres per hour. The unit depends on the measurement system used.
asks: What are the units for velocity?
Do I use metres or kilometres for speed?

facts: Distance is a scalar quantity, meaning it only has size.
Displacement is a vector quantity, meaning it has both size and direction.
Average velocity equals total displacement divided by total time.
Speed is the rate of change of distance, while velocity is the rate of change of displacement.

quiz.say: A runner completes one lap around a 400 metre track and ends where they started. What is their displacement?
quiz.why: Because the runner started and finished at the exact same point, the change in position, or displacement, is zero.

wrong.0: This is the total distance travelled, not the change in position.
wrong.1: This might be the distance if they ran twice around the track.
wrong.2: We know the start and end points are the same, so the displacement must be zero.

quiz.say: A car travels 10 metres east and then 10 metres west. What is its total displacement?
quiz.why: The movement east is cancelled out by the equal movement west, bringing it back to the starting point.

wrong.1: This is the total distance covered, ignoring the direction change.
wrong.2: This only considers the first part of the journey.
wrong.3: This only considers the second part of the journey.

quiz.say: If an object moves 50 metres in 10 seconds, what is its average velocity?
quiz.why: Average velocity is total displacement divided by time. Fifty metres divided by ten seconds is five metres per second.

wrong.0: This confuses the time taken with the final average speed.
wrong.1: This forgets to include the required unit of time, seconds.
wrong.3: This incorrectly multiplies the distance by the time taken.
